report.verdict: 🔴 Not safe to ship: 2 critical issue(s) need fixing now.
report.plain_summary: Your system has two serious weaknesses that could let an attacker take control if left unfixed. Three issues have already been fixed, and four smaller ones need to be watched. The biggest risks are unsafe file handling, a secret key left in the code, and not properly checking the partner connection.

items.title: OS Command Injection
items.plain: If a user can control the name of the file being compressed, they could trick the system into running malicious commands on the server, potentially taking full control of it.

items.title: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle)
items.plain: If an attacker can send a specially crafted file to be processed, the system will automatically run the malicious code hidden inside it, leading to a full system compromise.
items.fix: Use a safe format like JSON: import json; return json.loads(blob)

items.title: Hard-coded Credentials
items.plain: The secret key to access the partner portal is written in plain text in the code. If anyone sees the code, they can steal this key and access sensitive data or perform actions on your behalf.

items.title: TLS Certificate Verification Disabled
items.plain: The system is not checking if it is talking to the real partner server. An attacker could intercept the communication and steal the data or inject fake information without you knowing.
items.fix: Remove `verify=False` or ensure it is only used in controlled testing environments with proper CA bundles.

items.title: Missing Timeout in HTTP Request
items.plain: If the partner server is slow or down, your application will wait forever, potentially freezing up and becoming unresponsive to other users.
items.fix: return requests.post(portal_url, files={"f": fh}, headers={"Authorization": PORTAL_TOKEN}, timeout=10)

recon_summary:
- **What it does:** Renders invoice emails and fetches foreign-exchange rates for a PatchPilot demo target.
- **Tech stack:** A small service with email rendering and an FX-rate fetcher, using intentionally pinned, outdated dependencies.
- **Attack surface:** Untrusted input enters via invoice data used in email rendering and external FX-rate API responses/URLs.
- **Riskiest component:** The FX-rate fetcher, because it handles external network data with vulnerable pinned dependencies and may enable SSRF or injection risks.
